 Others receiving votes:  Iowa 76, New Mexico 41, Cincinnati 11, Oregon State 10, South Carolina 8, Minnesota 7, USC 7, UTSA 1, Virginia Tech 1  
 Miami remains steady at No. 1
 The No. 1 team in the country fell to an unranked opponent each of the past two weeks, so the Hurricanes needed to be prepared to face unranked Pittsburgh. However, Miami (Fla.) dominated the Panthers, 52-23, solidifying its top spot in the rankings. 
 DARIAN. MALACHI. ELITE‼️ https://t.co/pTZB1LWqDy
— Miami Hurricanes Football (@CanesFootball) October 24, 2026 
 Quarterback Darian Mensah completed 31-of-37 passes for 387 yards and four touchdowns, leaving Week 8 with the highest quarterback rating of the season. The Hurricanes are now one of only three undefeated teams in college football. 
 BYU, Texas Tech suffer first losses in offensive battles
 BYU and Texas Tech were two of the last five undefeated teams heading into Week 8. However, after both teams suffered shocking losses to unranked opponents, BYU sits at No. 8 and Texas Tech at No. 13.
 Coming off a thrilling win against previous No. 2 Notre Dame in Week 7, the Cougars could not hang on against unranked UCF, 39-31. Both teams put together strong offensive performances, with each quarterback notching at least one rushing and two passing touchdowns. 
 The Red Raiders’ first loss came against Cincinnati, 37-24. Both teams recorded at least 400 yards of total offense. Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV went 19-of-30 for 172 yards four touchdowns and two interceptions, while Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond went 24-of-37 for 227 yards, no touchdowns and one interception. 
 UCLA, Utah stay perfect
 The Bruins and Utes join the Hurricanes as the final three undefeated teams of the college football season. Utah rises to No. 6, with UCLA right behind at No. 7.
 UCLA handled Michigan State with a 28-10 win in Pasadena that saw the Bruins rush for 245 yards, while limiting the Spartans to 47. 
 Utah, however, had a different storyline against then-No. 14 Houston. Last week, the Utes survived a third-quarter surge from unranked Colorado, and this week, they outlasted the Cougars. Houston dropped down to No. 18.
 Despite Utah quarterback Devon Damper throwing zero touchdowns and two interceptions, he rushed for 150 yards and two touchdowns.
 Texas rises, Ole Miss falls to No. 12
 Texas climbed to No. 11 after defeating then-No. 6 Ole Miss 34-27 in Austin, marking the biggest leap in the poll this week. 
 The Longhorns managed to keep their playoff hopes alive, after losing to unranked teams in consecutive weeks. Texas built a 24-3 lead at the half, but Ole Miss responded with 21 unanswered points. The Rebels recovered their own onside kick with 1:20 on the clock, but an interception in the end zone sealed the victory for the Longhorns. 
 OLE MISS FALLS SHORT WITH NO TIME REMAINING. TEXAS WINS. https://t.co/VdX3dg0A5U
— ESPN (@espn) October 25, 2026 
 Despite shaky performances over the past two weeks, Texas quarterback Arch Manning went 18-of-30 for 212 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions — but he added two rushing touchdowns. Ole Miss quarterback and Heisman contender Trinidad Chambliss finished 25-of-52 for 250 yards for two touchdowns and three interceptions.
 Kentucky and Alabama enter top 10
 The Wildcats and Crimson Tide round out the top 10, respectively, after both teams added another conference win to their resumes.
 Kentucky is now 7-1 on the season, following its 34-17 win over Vanderbilt. The Commodores started fast with a 10-0 lead but could not stop the Wildcats, as quarterback Kenny Minchey completed 19-of-26 passes for 203 yards, and added both passing and rushing touchdowns. 
 Alabama topped Texas A&M 31-20 in a game that saw Aggie quarterback Marcel Reed get picked off twice. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell completed 19-of-30 passes for 311 yards with three touchdowns and one interception to seal the victory.
 Tennessee falls to No. 16, Iowa drops out
 Both the Volunteers and Hawkeyes entered Week 8 with one loss, and both left with their second. Tennessee drops to No. 16, with Iowa dropping out completely, after both teams lost to unranked opponents on walk-off field goals.
 Tennessee, previously ranked No. 11, faced unranked South Carolina on Saturday night in a game that saw the Volunteers score three rushing touchdowns in a 27-24 loss. The Gamecocks now have two top 25 wins under their belt, after defeating then-No. 16 Florida last week and upsetting Tennessee. 
 GAMECOCKS WIN https://t.co/3KE5wxUnF1
— South Carolina Football (@GamecockFB) October 24, 2026 
 Iowa used both Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski at quarterback in its 13-10 loss to Minnesota. The Hawkeyes' sole loss heading into last night came against then-No. 5 Ohio State back in Week 5. Now at two losses, Iowa is out of the top 25.
 Southern California drops out, Wisconsin enters 
 Southern California suffered its second loss of the season, this time to unranked Wisconsin, 24-7. Despite USC quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing for 258 yards compared to the 58 yards from Wisconsin's Colton Joseph, the Trojans could not find their rhythm in the run game, finishing with negative 17 total rushing yards.
 Another round of applause for our defense 👏 https://t.co/b3MJkCAMeX
— Wisconsin Football (@BadgerFootball) October 25, 2026 
 Wisconsin enters the AP Top 25 Poll for the first time this season at No. 25. The Badgers now have two top 25 wins on the season, with their first coming in Week 4 against then-No. 13 Penn State
